subject: chemistry-2
question: Which statement correctly defines molarity, and what is the molarity of a solution containing 0.5 mol of glucose in a total volume of 2 L?

options.text: Moles of solute per kilogram of solvent; the molarity is 0.25 M
Grams of solute per liter of solution; the molarity is 0.25 M
Moles of solute per liter of solution; the molarity is 0.25 M
Moles of solute per liter of solution; the molarity is 4 M

explanation:
Molarity (M) is moles of solute divided by liters of final solution, so 0.5 mol / 2 L = 0.25 M. Choice A gives the definition of molality (mol solute per kg solvent), a distinct unit used for colligative-property work; choice D applies the right definition but inverts the division (2 / 0.5). Molarity is referenced to the finished solution volume rather than the volume of solvent added, because dissolving a solute changes the final volume of the mixture.

ELI-10: Molarity answers one question: how many moles of solute sit in each liter of the finished liquid? Two details carry all the weight. First, the numerator is moles, not grams, so a mass must be converted before you can use it. Second, the denominator is the volume after mixing, not the volume of water you started with. Here, 0.5 mol spread over 2 L means each liter holds only a quarter of a mole, so the value is 0.25 M. If you ever get a number larger than the moles you started with, check that you did not divide backwards.
